risk_limits: Scheduler scan timeout is 30 seconds. The exact AbortSignal reaches the database query; a late non-cooperative response is prevented from changing the registry.
Stopping the scheduler prevents new timer callbacks. It cannot retract a queue submission already started or cancel a job already accepted by the queue.
Unit tests substitute database and queue dependencies. Three tests use real installed node-cron timers and registry.
No live Supabase, Redis, provider, email, payment, production migration, deployment or real mission was exercised.
Full KARTA suite was not rerun for this narrow change; scoped neighboring tests, whole KARTA typecheck and build passed.
GitNexus call-graph impacts were LOW before edits. Full-text search was unavailable and process graph was capped; absence of a graph path is not proof of absence.
Core worker execution, model routing, financial rules and existing CI are outside this patch.

analysis_anomaly.handling: Publication paused. The generated index was preserved, then rebuilt from scratch without editing product source or instructions. Qualified UID and enclosing-parent queries now resolve to the actual scheduler function and LOW risk. The specific internal cause of the earlier missing target id/type was not proven.
